summary: Pier Gabriele Goidanich was a linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore and under Graziadio Isaia Ascoli at the University of Milan. He served as professor at the University of Pisa and later held professorships at the University of Bologna.

Piero Martinetti was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin and at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano, the University of Milan, and Turin.
Pierre Arènes is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under André Bareau. He was affiliated with the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

Pierre Bourdieu was a philosopher and sociologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University, the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and the Collège de France.

Pierre Chantraine was a linguist who studied under Alfred Ernout, Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Theodor Bloch. He served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and as a professor at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.
Pierre Charles Olloba d'Ochoa was an Indologist who studied under Garcin de Tassy at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in 1839.

Pierre Dupont was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Charles Picard, and Moritz Abraham Stern. He held positions at the Guimet Museum, École française d'Extrême-Orient, National Museum of Vietnamese History, EPHE, and the Sorbonne.

Pierre Fabricius worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying under Heinrich Zimmer, Walther Schubring, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Renou across Heidelberg, Hamburg, and London. He later served as a professor at the Royal University of Phnom Penh (1965–1974).

Pierre Fallon was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at KU Leuven and the University of Calcutta. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, served as Professor of French Literature at the University of Calcutta, and founded Shanti Bhavan and Shanti Sadan.

Pierre Herman Leonard Eggermont was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Frederik David Kan Bosch and studied under several French scholars. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam and as professor at KU Leuven.

Pierre Johanns worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, educated at KU Leuven and the University of Oxford. He taught philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai and St. Mary's College, Kurseong, and taught Sanskrit at the University of Namur.

Pierre Meile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Visva-Bharati University under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and others. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from 1939 to 1963.

Pierre Rolland was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Paris, Aix-Marseille University, and in Germany under Karl Hoffmann, Louis Renou, and Armand Minard. In 1969, he became a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

Pierre-Amédée Jaubert was a linguist and Iranian studies scholar who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Institut d'Égypte, École des langues orientales, and Collège de France, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.
Pierre-Gustave Garrez was an Indologist who completed studies at the Lycée Henri-IV and the Lycée Louis-le-Grand.

Pierre-Philippe Giraudeau was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris and became a missionary with the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1877.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou. He worked with the French Institute of Pondicherry and the EFEO, held the Chair of Sanskrit at the EPHE, and served as Vice-President of the Société Asiatique.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics who completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University, where he also served as a research fellow (attested 1996).

Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology who earned his doctorate under Frederik David Kan Bosch at Leiden University. He served as a curator at the National Museum of Ethnology and as professor of museology at Leiden.
Pieter Jacob Cosijn was a linguist who studied at Utrecht University from around 1859 to 1865 and subsequently held an academic post at Leiden University from 1877 to 1899.
